svg.title: Q-NEXUS: how work flows
svg.desc: 1. Register the tender (KTT): Records the client tender, appoints the MQS and GM Engineering, and dates the seven stages up to the submission deadline. 2. Build the team (MQS, GM Engineering): The MQS adds QS and SCM staff, the GM Engineering adds the KTD and engineers, and each procurement gets its persons in charge. 3. Release the RFQ List (KTD): Lists the RFQs for the tender, where one row is one RFQ and one procurement, and releases the list so Engineering is notified. 4. Prepare the BOQ (Engineering): Fills in the bill of quantities and the attachments vendors will receive, then submits the RFQ to the KTD. 5. Approve the RFQ (KTD): Approves the RFQ, which moves the procurement to stage 2, or returns it with a required note. 6. Set the Initial Price (QS): Optionally prepares a reference price per item, with help from past tender and project prices in the Price Database. 7. Send the request for quotation (SCM): Picks vendors matched by category; blacklisted vendors and vendors without a valid email cannot be chosen, and the system builds the BOQ file for vendors. 8. Record quotations (SCM): Records each reply against the BOQ revision it answers; Excel offers are read by code and PDF or Word offers by an AI agent whose numbers must appear in the document. 9. Technical evaluation (Engineering): Rates each quotation as meeting the specification, needing clarification or not meeting it, and scores the TBE matrix item by item. 10. Commercial evaluation (QS): Rates the price as reasonable or not; a quotation becomes FINAL only when both the technical and the commercial gate are met. 11. Clarification (Engineering or QS, then SCM): The evaluator drafts the question, SCM sends it to the vendor and records the answer, and the evaluation reopens. 12. Negotiation (SCM, QS): SCM opens negotiation on FINAL quotations and records each round, QS validates every round and records the result. 13. Recommendation and selected vendor (System, QS): The system ranks FINAL quotations by 60% price and 40% technical score, and QS may mark one selected vendor with a written reason. 14. Close and archive (KTT): Closes the procurement as Completed, Failed, Canceled or Merged, uploads final documents, and the procurement stops accepting changes.
svg.text: From the first step to the last, and who does what.
